subject: MAP adjustment request — proposed buffer matrix + wrap-up asks
messages:
From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@horizonhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP status — risk on close date (need options)

Hi Irene / Grace,

Quick note from this morning's internal sync — procurement sign-off is slipping due to our third-party security attestation queue. Our current target of 2028-07-14 is at risk; PM estimates a 7–10 business day delay unless we can provide a narrower acceptance window or an exec-level signal to prioritize the attestation.

Can your team propose a short list of options we can present to procurement today? Useful deliverables would be: a) an adjusted MAP that shows an acceptance window with minimal rollback impact, b) proposed buffer / credit constructs if we need to buy time, and c) an explicit escalation path.

I appreciate anything you can get back by EOD PT.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Tran
Senior Product Manager, Horizon Health

Attachments referenced: none in this note.

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP status — risk on close date (need options)

Alyssa —

Thanks for the heads up. We're aligned on the problem and have three practical options ready for your procurement team to consider:

1) Compressed acceptance window (preferred) — move final acceptance to a 48-hour window starting 2028-07-19; we commit to prioritized engineering support and an automated rollback plan if acceptance criteria fail.

2) Buffer + conditional credit — keep the current acceptance date but pre-authorize a 10% transient credit (applied if acceptance slips beyond 5 business days) and provide a 2-week staging window for security attestations.

3) Canary cutover with scoped feature gating — deliver core integration on 2028-07-14 and gate higher-risk features to a secondary release on 2028-07-28.

I've attached a revised MAP (Horizon_MAP_v3.xlsx) that shows each option, an estimated cost delta, and the operational steps. Also attaching a one-page "close buffer matrix" (close_buffer_matrix.pdf) that maps triggers to recommended actions.

If procurement wants an exec signal, we can escalate to a short approval note from our SVP; Markus, can you advise on the minimum language you need to make that signal acceptable to legal/compliance?

Irene Choi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Horizon_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), close_buffer_matrix.pdf (one-pager)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP status — risk on close date (need options)

Alyssa — thank you. Quick note: option 1 is operationally cleanest for both teams (short acceptance window + prioritized support). Option 2 will buy time but adds billing complexity; we'd need a documented credit mechanic and sign-off.

Alyssa, if procurement prefers the buffer approach we can draft the credit language and an acceptance rollback runbook today.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP status — proposed buffer matrix + compliance approval language

Irene / Grace / Alyssa —

Markus from Legal here. For an exec-level prioritization signal we need a short, neutral commitment that does not create open-ended liability. Suggested minimal language: "Redwood will prioritize Horizon Health's security attestation processing and provide a dedicated point of contact; if any regressions are found during acceptance, Redwood will execute the rollback plan documented in the MAP."
If you want a credit mechanic, propose the exact trigger (e.g., "acceptance not completed within 5 business days of target") and the credit cap (we typically limit credits to a percentage of the first-month committed spend). I can draft the clause once you confirm numbers.

Also attaching a quick snapshot of our risk log that maps the attestation queue to downstream acceptance exposures — please see risk_log_snapshot.csv.

Markus Klein
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: risk_log_snapshot.csv (CSV)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@horizonhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP status — executive note and temporary buffer approval

Alyssa / team —

I've reviewed the options. For Horizon Health (HL-4729) I'm OK with option 2 (Buffer + conditional credit) as a temporary measure to keep the project moving while compliance completes their queue. Two asks from my side: 1) cap the credit at 10% of the first-month invoice and 2) set a hard sunset of 30 calendar days for the buffer mechanics.

Irene / Markus: please draft the short exec note (see Markus' suggested language) and the credit clause with the caps above. Grace: coordinate with procurement on which acceptance triggers procurement will accept as "satisfied" so we can avoid churn.

Alyssa: if procurement can confirm acceptance triggers by EOD tomorrow we will prepare the DocuSign for the buffer amendment.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
